findings.proposed: (this locale's string unchanged) — pin the renderer: teamBridgeEventOwnerConsent returns true only when line.targets.length === 1, so a rolled-up consent keeps ui.teamBridge.events.consented, which reads correctly with a list here
findings.detail: A consent roll-up (two records sharing one request_id — the grouping key team-bridge-member-events-model.ts:144-156 groups on) produces one line with two targets, and the owner arm renders the possessive singular over the pair: « Sana Ketabchi autorizó la entrada de su agente Aida (Sana Ketabchi) y Scout (Sana Ketabchi) » — singular « su agente » with a coordinated pair. English has the same defect ("their agent A and B"), so this is not a translation error: the sentence's grammatical number depends on a cardinality nothing enforces, and the en sidecar's "always exactly one name for this key" is that unenforced assumption. « sus agentes A y B » is the plural form, but it cannot be selected from a pre-joined string; the cardinality guard is the fix. Reachability: the UI merges these events itself; whether the hub emits two consent records under one request_id is unverified (the server is not deployed and no corpus is readable here).

findings.proposed: if (line.actor.kind !== "human") return false;  /* before the every() test; the cardinality guard is CO-B1 */
findings.detail: The predicate compares account ids but never the actor's kind. An agent party carries its OWNER's account_id (the contract's own statement, restated in the model's docstring), so a consent whose actor is an agent on the same account takes the owner arm and the sentence claims a relation an agent cannot have. Executed: actor = agent "Aida (Sana Ketabchi)", target = agent "Scout (Sana Ketabchi)" renders Aida (Sana Ketabchi) autorizó la entrada de su agente Scout (Sana Ketabchi) — for this locale the self-approval reading the audit was asked about becomes possible only through this hole, never through the wording. Minor: no readable corpus proves the hub records an agent as the consenting actor; the guard costs one line and makes the predicate match its own docstring ("the actor owns the target").

findings.detail: The sibling now renders whenever the owner arm's predicate is false — the non-owner case, a mixed group, and (once CO-B1 is fixed) any multi-target group — so its sidecar still tells the next translator the key is the owner's line and invites a possessive into the arm that is designed to claim no relation. This locale's sibling value (Sana Ketabchi autorizó la entrada de Aida (Sana Ketabchi)) already claims none; only the English context is stale.
